JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed U/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a RTA.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that on 28.02.2024 at about 7.45 p.m, the deceased was proceeding as pedestrian by observing all the traffic rules and regulations on the footpath of the Gulur road in front of Bakery, near Gulur Circle, Bagapalli Town and Taluk, Chikkaballapura District, at that time the driver of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AA- 6393 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and dashed to the deceased.
Due to the impact the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body and succumbed to the fatal injuries on the spot.

Postmortem was conducted at Bagepalli Government Hospital and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies and they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.

It is contended that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tipper Lorry and as such both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he placed exparte.
4. The respondent No.2 filed objections statement and denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Tipper Lorry.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Non -compliance of section 134(c), 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of tipper lorry is denied by this respondent.
Per contra it is alleged that the accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased who without observing the traffic rules and regulations.
Hence there is a contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of Tipper lorry did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :

REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.2: The petitioners have knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.50 lakhs together.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by son of deceased, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of Tipper Lorry for the offences punishable under section's 279, 304(A) of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondent No.2 has denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioners.
Therefore, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Tipper Lorry.
With this observation issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative.
9. ISSUE NO.1 :
The petitioners claim that petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are the major son and married daughter of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit-in-lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhaar cards of petitioners and deceased and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.

In a recent decision in National Insurance Company Limited v.
Birender [(2020) 11 SCC 356], a claim petition filed by major married and earning sons of the deceased mother, the Honourable Supreme Court held as follows:
"12.

Birender [(2020) 11 SCC 356]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166 (1).
The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependent on the deceased would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.

This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra)
had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
14. It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.

The evidence on record in the present case would suggest that the claimants were working as agricultural labourers on contract basis and were earning meager income between Rs. 1,00,000/and Rs. 1,50,000/per annum.
In that sense, they were largely dependent on the earning of their mother and in fact, were staying with her, who met with an accident at the young age of 48 years."

Therefore, in view of the principles laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala and Hon'ble Supreme Court, which is referred in the above decision, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the major married / earning sons and married daughters are also dependents to the deceased and they are entitled for the compensation under the motor vehicles accident cases.
It is pertinent to note that, this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased was not disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers to issue No.1 In the Affirmative.

13. The counsel for respondent No.2 filed written arguments and argued that the deceased would have retired from service after the completion of two months from the date of accident.
Hence the Split multiplier has to be considered instead of considering multiplier of "9".
The deceased would retire from the service of attaining his superannuation at the age of 60 years.
The deceased would get only pensionary income but not 100% of the salary.
Therefore, deceased remaining of service for two months net salary need to be taken after deducting personal tax and Tax deduction at source.
Thereafter the deceased would get 50% of his salary as pension.
Further while awarding loss of dependency 50% of the deceased salary needs to be considered and also personal expenses to be deducted.
Further the deceased son has been appointed to government job under compassionate grounds, therefore there is no loss of dependency.

In support of this contention the respondent No.2 has relied on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka , Dharwad Bench in the case of (i)

In the case on hand the deceased was aged 59 years.
His income is taken as Rs.33,178/- p.m.
In this case the deceased being an employee of the State Government had a permanent job.
Therefore as per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SC 5157, 15% of income is to be added towards future prospects.
15% of Rs.33,178/- works out to Rs.4,977/-.
Therefore the total income comes to Rs.38,155/- (33,178 + 4,977).
There are three dependents.
Hence 1/3rd is to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
1/3rd of Rs.38,155/- works out to Rs.12,718/-.
Income for consideration is Rs.25,437/- (38,155 - 12,718).
Annual income works out to Rs.3,05,244/- (25,437 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '9'.
Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.27,47,196/- (Rs.3,05,244 X 9) which is rounded off to Rs.27,47,200/-.
